questions.q: How many mandatory seasonal releases does Salesforce ship per year, and who controls when a specific org receives them?
options: Four releases a year, and the customer chooses the exact date
One release a year, scheduled entirely by the customer's release manager
Three releases a year (Spring, Summer, Winter), on a schedule Salesforce sets and publishes, not the customer
Releases happen continuously with no fixed names or schedule at all
questions.explain: Salesforce ships three named seasonal releases a year — Spring, Summer, and Winter — and every org is upgraded on a schedule Salesforce sets and publishes in advance; the customer doesn't choose the date.

questions.q: What is the sandbox preview window?
options: The period before a seasonal release reaches production where sandboxes get the new release early so teams can test against it
A permanent setting that disables all sandboxes during a seasonal release
A tool that lets an org skip a seasonal release entirely
The 180-day period Setup Audit Trail entries are retained
questions.explain: The sandbox preview window is the testing opportunity Salesforce provides by upgrading eligible sandboxes to the new seasonal release ahead of the production upgrade.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is a Release Update?
options: A synonym for a seasonal release itself, with no separate meaning
A change that always takes effect immediately with no advance notice
A change only developers can see, never visible to admins
An individually tracked platform change, introduced in a seasonal release, that goes through its own enable/enforce lifecycle with a published future enforcement date
questions.explain: Unlike the seasonal release as a whole, a Release Update is tracked individually, shows a status such as not-yet-enabled or enforced, and gives admins a window to test and enable it ahead of a published enforcement date.

questions.q: Where does this lesson say an admin should look to find the authoritative upgrade dates for a specific org?
options: A third-party blog post, since Salesforce doesn't publish this information itself
The Trust Status site, by looking up the org's specific instance
The org's Setup Audit Trail
The Salesforce AppExchange listing page
questions.explain: The lesson identifies Trust Status (status.salesforce.com / Salesforce's Trust area) as the authoritative, instance-specific source for an org's maintenance and upgrade windows.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend a change-freeze window around a seasonal production upgrade weekend?
options: Because if something breaks right after a seasonal upgrade, avoiding your own risky deployment that same week makes it easier to tell whether the platform upgrade or your own release caused the problem
Because Salesforce legally requires all customer deployments to stop during that week
Because sandboxes are unavailable during that week
Because change freezes are required only for declarative changes, never for Apex
questions.explain: The lesson frames the freeze window as a practical risk-isolation practice: avoiding your own large releases during the platform's own upgrade week makes it much easier to diagnose the real cause if something goes wrong.
